name: Tart + Orchard (Cirrus Labs)

modes.label: Self-hosted licence on your own Macs (compute not included)
modes.note: Software licence only: Tart (Apple Virtualization.framework VM manager) + Orchard orchestrator. You bring and pay for the Macs (e.g. Scaleway / MacStadium / AWS EC2 Mac). vcpu_h/ram_gib_h = 0 means "no compute charge from Tart", not free compute. All P+E host cores count toward the licence.

plans.name: Free Tier
plans.note: Current Tart/Orchard releases are under FSL-1.1-ALv2 (relicensed 2026-06-05, copyright OpenAI): free for any internal use with no core/worker caps; prohibited only for a 'Competing Use' (offering it in a commercial product/service that substitutes for the Software). Each release converts to Apache-2.0 two years after it is made available. tart.run/licensing still prints the old 100-core / 4-worker Fair Source tiers (stale page). Older releases (pre-June 2026) remain under the Fair Source licence text.

plans.name: Gold
plans.note: $12,000 per year; 500 cores / 20 Orchard workers; priority support. Bought via licensing@cirruslabs.org. LEGACY: Cirrus Labs "stopped charging licensing fees" for Tart/Orchard after agreeing to join OpenAI (cirruslabs.org, 2026-04-07); tart.run/licensing still lists the tier.

plans.name: Platinum
plans.note: $36,000 per year; 3,000 cores / 200 Orchard workers. LEGACY: Cirrus Labs "stopped charging licensing fees" for Tart/Orchard after agreeing to join OpenAI (cirruslabs.org, 2026-04-07); tart.run/licensing still lists the tier.

plans.name: Diamond
plans.note: $12 per CPU core per year, unlimited Orchard workers. LEGACY: Cirrus Labs "stopped charging licensing fees" for Tart/Orchard after agreeing to join OpenAI (cirruslabs.org, 2026-04-07); tart.run/licensing still lists the tier.

caveats: Not a hosted service: the engine must add the cost of the Macs you run it on. Plan fees are yearly licences shown as /12.

Licence is FSL-1.1-ALv2 (Functional Source License, source-available; each release becomes Apache-2.0 after 2 years). open_source true in the loose sense. Competing Use (reselling it as a substitute commercial product/service) is not permitted.
Examples inside the Free Tier: 12 Mac minis x 8 cores running up to 24 VMs; 13 Mac minis exceed it.

Status (verified 2026-09-28, cirruslabs.org): Cirrus Labs agreed to join OpenAI (2026-04-07); Cirrus CI shut down 2026-06-01; Cirrus Runners closed to new customers; Tart/Vetu/Orchard to be relicensed under a more permissive licence and "we have also stopped charging licensing fees". Paid tiers flagged legacy. The software itself is not discontinued, so the self-hosted regime is not flagged legacy; future maintenance is uncertain.
Apple macOS SLA: leasing a Mac requires a minimum lease of 24 consecutive hours with sole use by the lessee, and allows at most 2 additional macOS VMs per Mac.
Software licence only: you supply and pay for the Mac hardware, so the estimate excludes compute.
Never has a compute price: no_price_reason "software licence only - bring your own Macs" (needs engine support to surface instead of the generic "no usable compute price").
Project is actively maintained under OpenAI's GitHub org (github.com/openai/tart; releases 2.38.0-2.40.0 on 2026-09-24..28).
no_price_reason: software licence only - bring your own Macs

fleet.tiers: No licence tiers for current releases (FSL-1.1-ALv2, no core/worker caps for internal use). Fleet size bounded only by your Mac hardware and Apple's 2-extra-macOS-VMs-per-Mac SLA.
fleet.notes: Self-hosted software, not provisioned compute. Host-core/worker licence restrictions must not be encoded as guest VM or vCPU quota; fleet also requires owned/rented Apple hardware.
